newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark to hold EU referendum in early 1998.
newsitem.headline: Denmark to hold EU referendum in early 1998.

text.p: Denmark will probably hold a referendum early in 1998 on the results of crucial EU talks because of a court battle over the legality of its EU membership, a government minister said on Monday.

"I find it difficult to see Denmark ratifying the results of the current IGC (Inter-Governmental Conference) before the High Court constitutional case is completed," Danish economy minister Marianne Jelved told journalists.
"I reckon that Denmark will hold a referendum on the results of IGC in the first six months of next year," she said.

The Danish High Court is to start proceedings next month on a suit filed by 10 Danes claiming that the handover of some political and judicial powers to EU institutions breaches Denmark's constitution.
A government defeat in court could oblige Denmark to renegotiate its EU treaties from scratch or try to amend the constitution, a complex operation requiring a general election and a referendum.
The IGC is a series of conferences to overhaul the Maastricht Treaty and review the 15-member EU's institutions before expected expansion eastward over the next 10 years.
Ministers want to trim the size of the executive European Commission and extend the scope of qualified majority voting.

Some seek to integrate the Western European Union (WEU), the bloc's fledgling defence club, into the EU, creating a collective security policy. But the bloc's four neutral states, plus Britain, are likely to resist a Franco-German-led plan for a phased move to a common defence policy.
Also on the agenda is a bid to cut the EU's 18 million jobless roster by writing job creation goals into a revamped treaty.
The schedule to revise the Maastricht accord is tight.

Unless the IGC review is completed by a June summit of EU leaders, talks with those wanting to join the bloc risk being pushed aside by preparations for the 1999 start of economic and monetary union (EMU) and by next year's French and German elections.
Denmark joined the EU in 1973 but Danes have always been cool towards European integration.

They rejected the Maastricht Treaty in a 1992 referendum and only accepted it in a second vote in 1993, on condition that Denmark opt out of economic and monetary union and joint defence, citizenship and asylum policy.
